concepts.learning_objective: Identify natural and synthetic acid-base indicators and use their colour changes to tell acids from bases.
Explain how olfactory indicators such as vanilla, onion and clove oil show acids and bases by a change in odour.

topics.title: Chemical reactions of acids and bases

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the reactions of acids and of bases with metals, and the test for the hydrogen gas evolved.
Predict the products when metal carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids and test for carbon dioxide.
Explain neutralisation and classify metallic oxides as basic and non-metallic oxides as acidic.

topics.title: What all acids and all bases have in common

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that acids produce H+(aq) ions only in water, which makes their solutions conduct electricity.
Recognise that H+ ions exist as hydronium ions and that bases give OH- ions, soluble bases being alkalis.
Explain why dissolving acids or bases in water is exothermic and why acid must be added to water.

topics.title: Strength of acid and base solutions: the pH scale

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the pH value of a solution to its hydrogen ion concentration and its acidic, neutral or basic nature.
Distinguish strong and weak acids by the amount of H+ ions they produce at the same concentration.

topics.title: Importance of pH in everyday life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of pH in the body, digestion, acid rain and soil for plant growth.
Apply neutralisation to explain tooth decay prevention and remedies for bee and nettle stings.

topics.title: Salts: families, pH and chemicals from common salt

concepts.learning_objective: Group salts into families by their common positive or negative radicals.
Predict whether a salt solution is acidic, basic or neutral from the strength of its parent acid and base.
Describe the chlor-alkali process and the preparation and uses of bleaching powder.

topics.title: Baking soda, washing soda and water of crystallisation

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the preparation, reactions and uses of baking soda and washing soda.
Define water of crystallisation and explain the colour change of copper sulphate crystals on heating.
Explain the formation, setting and storage of Plaster of Paris from gypsum.
